# The door register

**Status:** measured artifact, regenerated by gate. **Gate:** `npm run door-register:check` (fast lane). **Machine-readable:** [`door-register.json`](./door-register.json).

A **door** is any rule in this pipeline that decides a computed fact is NOT a fact of this component (*subtractive*) or that a fact IS admitted (*admitting*). Doors are the only judgement calls the conversion makes. Everything else is mechanical.

This register names **425** doors across ten stages, states the PREMISE each one assumes about the page it is measuring, says what it subtracts or admits, gives a counter-example where the premise is or could be false, and records whether the door leaves a receipt when it fires.

## Why this exists

The two worst defects found on the corpus had the same shape.

> **shadcn Input, invisible.** shadcn ships `* { border-color: var(--border) }` globally. The capture harness renders its control elements *inside the same page*, so the bare `<span>` control carries `oklch(0.922 0 0)` too. The Input's real `border-top-color` therefore compared EQUAL to the control and was dropped as "not a fact of this component" — while `border-top-width: 1px` (`0px` on the control) shipped. A 1px border with no colour paints nothing.

> **Polaris text, inkless.** The provider sets `color` on an ancestor. The control inherits it from the same page. The component's ink compared EQUAL and was dropped. The generated surface has no provider, so the text drew black — or nothing.

Neither loss produced a single line anywhere. The rule that made both calls was a bare `if` in `extract/computed/fuse.ts`:

```ts
if (a.baseFlat[pi].node.style[p] !== ctrl[p]) set.add(p);
```

The premise — *a value the bare control also has is the user agent's or the library's reset, and the emitted DOM inherits it for free* — is right most of the time and catastrophically wrong whenever the library's **global** CSS supplies the value, because the emitted CSS reproduces the component's rules and not the page's.

**Both losses are now closed.** `ctrl[p]` has become `baseline(p)`: the control is measured on a page carrying the browser, the colour-scheme and the stage box and nothing the library ships, so a page-global rule can no longer cancel a fact by landing on the probe. The corpus carries 4,418 fewer subtractions and shadcn's library-authored drops fall from 103 to 1. The two defects above are pinned as conformance cases `page-global-star-rule` and `page-inherited-ink`, and `capture.control-baseline-mint` — the door whose false premise minted the polluted probe — records what its nodes are still used for.

The point of this register is that a judgement call which is not written down is not reviewable. The register round itself changed what no door carries; the baseline round that followed it changed exactly one, deliberately, and re-measured every count in this document.

## The marker convention

Every registered door is marked at its deciding rule:

```ts
// @door fuse.control-element-delta
if (v !== baseline(p)) set.add(p);
```

`npm run door-register:check` refuses when a `@door` marker exists in code with no register entry (a new judgement call nobody wrote down), when a registered door has no marker (the register drifted off its rule), when a registered line is not where the marker sits, and when a door **claims** a receipt whose receipt path does not exist in its own file. A register that claims honesty it does not have is worse than one that admits silence.

## What the doors subtract, measured

All 116 committed components are re-fused through this tree's engine — no browser, the same offline replay `regate.ts` uses — and every receipt is bucketed by door. `npx tsx scripts/door-census.ts`.

| library | components | control-equal drops | of those, **library-authored** | span-fallback parts | other door firings (receipted) | code-only residue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| altitude | 8 | 4,734 | **6** | 5 | 85 | 21 |
| antd | 12 | 25,048 | **23** | 20 | 325 | 113 |
| astryx | 10 | 23,321 | **0** | 16 | 359 | 306 |
| carbon | 10 | 37,271 | **12** | 32 | 603 | 189 |
| fluent | 11 | 20,892 | **13** | 19 | 336 | 128 |
| mui | 31 | 70,062 | **0** | 93 | 1,185 | 424 |
| polaris | 12 | 44,659 | **69** | 43 | 765 | 320 |
| shadcn | 11 | 12,244 | **1** | 7 | 219 | 107 |
| tailwind | 11 | 8,087 | **9** | 7 | 118 | 47 |
| **total** | **116** | **246,318** | **133** | **242** | **3,995** | **1,655** |

**Reading it.** `control-equal drops` is every `(part, channel)` the control-element delta door subtracted — 246,318 of them, and until this round *every single one was silent*. Most are genuine initial values; the count is here so the surface can never again look like zero.

`library-authored` is the subset the library's **own stylesheet** declares on that element — proven by the capture reader's own `vrefs`, or by a `var()`-carrying shorthand recorded at the shorthand ceiling (`border-color: var(--input)` is only ever visible there). For those the door's premise is provably false. **That number — 133 — is the honest size of the "missing ink" surface**, and it is not evenly spread: Polaris (69) carries half of it.

**What this table measured before the UA baseline, and what changed.** The register's first census was taken while the control-element delta subtracted against the IN-PAGE control — the four bare elements the harness mounts in the same document as the component, which therefore inherit every page-global rule the library ships. Its totals were 250,736 drops and **244** library-authored, three quarters of them in shadcn (103) and Polaris (78) — exactly where the two named defects were found, by a measurement built without reference to them.

That door now subtracts against `uaControls` (`capture.captureUaControls`), a page carrying the browser, the colour-scheme and the stage box and nothing the library ships, and the census replay passes it. The 4,418 drops that disappeared are the page-global facts the door was cancelling; they are carried now. **shadcn falls 103 → 1** — the invisible-Input surface this census was built to size is closed — and Polaris falls 78 → 69.

One count RISES: **antd 19 → 23**. A channel whose authored value happens to coincide with the user agent's own default differed from the in-page control (which carried antd's global) and equals the UA control, so it is dropped now and was carried before. Those four channels are a real hole the fix opened, and this table counts them rather than absorbing them into the win.

`span-fallback parts` are parts whose tag has no rendered control at all (only `button`, `span`, `a` and `div` do), so the delta was taken against the wrong element in both directions. shadcn's Input is one of these: `<input>` measured against `<span>`.

astryx and MUI measure 0 library-authored drops because neither expresses component facts through CSS custom properties at the point of use (StyleX compiles them away; Emotion writes literals), so the reader has no `vrefs` evidence to split on. That is a limit of the discriminator, named here rather than reported as a clean bill.

**164 of 425 doors still fire silently.** They are listed as such below, per stage, and the count is gated: a register that claims every door receipts is refused.

### Closed this round

- **`anatomy.svg-currentcolor-fold`** (`extract/computed/anatomy.ts:1580`) — One line per discarded literal colour per asset, naming the value the fold threw away and the inherited colour it matched. The rewrite is unchanged.
- **`fuse.control-element-delta`** (`extract/computed/fuse.ts:861`) — One count line per part, plus one NAMED line per channel the library's own stylesheet declares on that element (control-equal-drop-authored) — the missing-ink surface, channel by channel. Since the UA-baseline round the door also receipts what it REFUSES to cancel: `page-global-baseline-corrected:` names every channel the in-page control would have subtracted and the UA baseline proves the library authored.
- **`gate.empty-comparison-is-100`** (`extract/computed/gate.ts:562`) — When cellsCompared is 0 the fabricated 100 now announces itself in the scorecard's namedLosses. The number is unchanged.

### The largest still-silent doors

Ranked by what a wrong firing costs, not by how often it fires:

- **`propose.is-spacer-elides-styling`** (`core/propose-figma.ts:7830`) — drops every styled channel of a node on a structural predicate; if the predicate ever misses `effects`, `cornerRadius`, `opacity` or `clipsContent`, they vanish with no receipt at all. The widest silent subtraction on the propose side.
- **`fuse.state-plane-residue-only-on-contract`** (`extract/computed/fuse.ts:3308`) — withholds EVERY base-plane refusal in the whole pipeline from `Part.codeOnly`, so `figma bundle`'s `codeOnlyFacts` — the only loss list a designer pasting a set ever sees — never mentions them.
- **`anatomy.boxless-wrapper-unwrap`** (`extract/computed/anatomy.ts:841`) — tests only `border-top-width` and `border-bottom-width`, so a wrapper with a left- or right-only border reads as boxless and is unwrapped away.
- **`propose.effect-state-preview-shadow`** (`core/propose-figma.ts:2862`) — the only bare `return;` on the propose side that subtracts a fully observed, fully carriable fact on a premise about *another door's* behaviour, with no note and no unbound row.
- **`libcss.missing-class-nonmatch`** (`extract/computed/lib-css.ts:320`) — `missingClasses` is computed as multi-axis evidence and then discarded entirely by its only consumer — the evidence never reaches `QueryOutcome`.
- **`capture.at-import-strip`** (`extract/computed/capture.ts:687`) — the `stripped` count is computed and thrown away by the destructure at the call site; a library whose whole token layer arrives via `@import` is captured against a page that never loaded it.
- **`gate.carried-parts-only`** (`extract/computed/gate.ts:389`) — three silent `return`s (`gate.carried-parts-only`, `gate.icon-part-exclusion`, `gate.unaligned-truth-el-skip`) shrink the score's denominator with no counter.

## The register

`kind` is **s** subtractive, **a** admitting, **b** both. `receipt` names the literal that proves the receipt path, or **silent**.

### capture — `extract/computed/capture.ts`

What the browser is asked, and what is thrown away before fusion ever sees it. Twenty-four of these rules live inside a serialized in-page function, so their `@door` marker sits on the nearest line outside the template literal and the register records the real rule line as `ruleLine`. 34 doors, 19 silent.

| `capture.class-allow-filter` | 1099<br/>*(rule 1107)* | s | A regex over classList keeps exactly the identity-bearing classes. | Drops every non-matching class from node.classes, reshaping signatures, stems and part names. | A library whose identity class does not match the prefix loses its part identity entirely. | **silent** |

### fusion — `extract/computed/fuse.ts`

The largest gauntlet: which computed channels are facts of this component at all. `fuse.control-element-delta` is the single biggest subtraction in the pipeline. 131 doors, 47 silent.

| door | line | kind | premise | subtracts / admits | counter-example | receipt |

CUSTOM PROPERTIES (`--*`) are the one deliberate narrowing: they keep the IN-PAGE baseline, because a `:root` token block inherits onto every element in the page and a custom property paints nothing on its own — the channels it FEEDS are what this door measures. | Drops EVERY admitted channel equal to that baseline. Still the single largest subtraction in the pipeline: 246,318 (part, channel) pairs across the committed corpus. A capture carrying no `uaControls` falls back to the in-page control and says so once per part (`ua-baseline-missing:`). | Two channels the UA baseline still cancels wrongly. (1) A library-authored value that COINCIDES with the user agent's own default equals the UA control and is dropped, even though the library declares it — 133 such drops corpus-wide, 23 of them in antd, which is 4 MORE than the in-page baseline dropped. (2) A `--*` custom property keeps the in-page baseline by construction, so one the library defines page-globally and the component re-declares identically is still dropped. The failure this door was named for — shadcn's `* { border-color: var(--border) }` cancelling the Input's real border-colour and Polaris' provider ink cancelling its text — is CLOSED by the UA baseline and pinned by the conformance cases `page-global-star-rule` and `page-inherited-ink`; shadcn's authored drops fell 103 to 1. | `control-equal-drop:` |

| `fuse.pair-over-two-unset-axes` | 3091<br/>*(rule 2975)* | s | No carried spelling exists for a product of two defaultless axes. | Drops the binding. | Two optional adornment axes together lose their colour. | `overflowBindings.push` |

| `fuse.text-part-typography-carried` | 988<br/>*(rule 948)* | a | Context-inherited typography IS the rendered truth; generated surfaces have no library body to inherit from. | Admits font-size/line-height/font-weight/font-family on text parts even when control-equal. | Deliberately unguarded by admit(), so it can re-add a channel the viewport door refused. | `text-part-typography-carried` |

| `fuse.tokens-by-prop-conflict-cross-field` | 3241<br/>*(rule 3119)* | s | The v14 no-two-entries rule spans tokensByProp and literalsByProp. | Drops the computed token. | A reviewed literal beats a measured token ref. | `enrichmentNotes.push` |
| `fuse.tokens-by-prop-conflict-same-field` | 3254<br/>*(rule 3131)* | s | Same rule, within tokensByProp. | Drops the computed token. | A stale reviewed map masks the measured one. | `enrichmentNotes.push` |
| `fuse.tokens-by-prop-reorder` | 3334<br/>*(rule 3208)* | a | resolveTokens merges in order and later wins, so defaultless-axis maps must sort after defaulted ones. | Admits the named plane over its own fallback. | Order is a convention the emitters must keep. | `enrichmentNotes.push` |

| `fuse.translate-door-refused` | 938<br/>*(rule 902)* | s | The bounded translate grammar covers every honest case; anything else is a non-translate transform. | Drops synthetic translate-x/y for that part entirely. | A rotate+translate thumb loses its motion. | `translate-door-refused` |
| `fuse.triage-named-cause` | 1613<br/>*(rule 1552)* | a | A config-declared triage rule turns a contradiction into an accepted, named cause. | Removes the row from untriaged so it stops blocking. | A triage rule written too broadly hides a real contradiction. | `r.cause = rule.cause` |
| `fuse.uncorrelated-overflow` | 2939<br/>*(rule 2833)* | s | A mint binding with a null ref is uncorrelated across planes. | Drops the token binding. | A three-axis colour loses its binding entirely. | `overflowBindings.push` |
| `fuse.uniform-or-nothing-absolute` | 172<br/>*(rule 168)* | a | A part is overlay anatomy only if position:absolute in EVERY enabled default combo. | Gates the whole geometry admission (width/height/insets/translate) for the cluster. | MUI Slider's thumb is static in one size variant, so the whole overlay cluster loses geometry. | **silent** |
| `fuse.uniform-ratio-not-a-fold` | 1298<br/>*(rule 1251)* | a | With only one observed font-size an em-fold is indistinguishable from a uniform value. | Admits (mints) a uniform px value rather than folding. | A single-size component's em tracking is minted as px and stops scaling. | **silent** |

| `fuse.unmintable-kind-residue` | 2330<br/>*(rule 2245)* | s | Only color/px/number/shadow/gradient shapes plus the declared registry are carriable. | Drops the channel as "no schema channel today" (705 corpus-wide). | Every genuinely new fact class lands here and stays. | `no schema channel today` |
| `fuse.viewport-anchored-translate-carried` | 558<br/>*(rule 538)* | a | No single-capture arithmetic proves a positioner-written translate is harness-coupled, so refusing would be a hunch. | Admits translate-x/y on a viewport-resolved part. | A tooltip positioner's harness offset is minted as design motion. | `viewport-anchored-translate-carried` |
| `fuse.viewport-derived-geometry-refused` | 536<br/>*(rule 517)* | s | A number that is a function of the harness window is not a library fact. | Drops left+right (+width) and top+bottom (+height) at every downstream door. | A genuinely full-bleed banner loses its width. | `viewport-derived-geometry-refused` |

| `fuse.zero-observation-part` | 2245<br/>*(rule 2168)* | s | A part with no element in ANY __default alignment is carried nowhere. | Drops every channel of that part. | An interaction-only part is carried on no plane at all. | `codeOnly.push` |

### token minting — `core/mint-tokens.ts`

When an observed value becomes a token, and under which name. 29 doors, 17 silent.

| door | line | kind | premise | subtracts / admits | counter-example | receipt |
|---|---:|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| `mint.alias-emitted-as-var` | 854<br/>*(rule 826)* | a | A shipped alias must stay a reference so the library's own stylesheet and modes still decide the value. | Admits a var() spelling. | Printed raw it is invalid CSS and a silent empty custom property; comment only. | **silent** |
| `mint.bool-axis-root-only` | 298<br/>*(rule 290)* | s | Bool sides are spelled as root data-attribute selectors, a spelling nested parts do not have. | Drops bool axes from every nested-part classification. | The filter is silent; only a terminal none gets a reason. | **silent** |
| `mint.distinct-value-hint` | 794<br/>*(rule 767)* | a | Heavy repetition across cells is structure an arbitrary assignment would not show. | Admits either way and annotates. | Deliberately a hint, not a gate. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.dtcg-type-omission` | 229<br/>*(rule 225)* | s | An unnameable value shape gets NO invented type rather than a wrong one. | Drops the type from sizing-keyword leaves. | Silently omitted. | **silent** |
| `mint.group-prefix-compatibility` | 708<br/>*(rule 683)* | s | The substituted ref must be a real tree prefix for every key, so suffixes are probed as a group. | Drops a group base. | Silent. | **silent** |
| `mint.leaf-under-leaf-fence` | 630<br/>*(rule 609)* | s | A leaf may not sit on another leaf's path because a group under a leaf would corrupt the DTCG tree. | Drops that path and retries with a suffix. | The retry is silent. | **silent** |
| `mint.namespace-fence` | 62 | a | No minted name may be mistaken for a semantic token. | Admits every minted path under imported.*. | The prefix is the receipt; there is no ledger line. | `imported.` |
| `mint.nested-pairs-opt-in` | 360<br/>*(rule 349)* | s | A caller whose binding placer cannot spell a nested pair must never be handed one. | Drops pair classification for nested parts when the flag is off. | A capable caller that forgets the flag loses pairs. | `reason` |
| `mint.nested-triple-refusal` | 529<br/>*(rule 511)* | s | A nested part's per-value map pins exactly one axis, leaving two placeholders. | Drops every nested triple. | A three-axis nested colour mints nothing. | `reason` |
| `mint.no-occurrences` | 290<br/>*(rule 284)* | s | An observation with no occurrences has nothing to mint. | Drops the observation. | None known. | `reason` |
| `mint.pair-full-coverage-first-pass` | 396<br/>*(rule 384)* | a | Every fully-covered pair must be tried before any relaxed pass, or axis order alone trades a measured binding for a supplied one. | Admits the two-axis classification. | Only surfaced via the unwitnessed caveat. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.path-claim-value-never-overwritten` | 632<br/>*(rule 610)* | a | A path claim with the same value and text style merges usage sites; a different value takes a numeric suffix. | Admits both and never overwrites a value. | The numeric suffix is the only trace; nothing names the collision. | **silent** |
| `mint.per-key-textstyle-fallback` | 724<br/>*(rule 698)* | a | A per-axis-value leaf takes the matching occurrence's style name, then the observation-level one, then none. | Admits an identity onto each axis leaf. | A wrong fallback attaches the wrong style name. | **silent** |
| `mint.ragged-fill-value-rank` | 497<br/>*(rule 481)* | a | The fill must be a function of the contract's declared axis order, never the dump's arbitrary first occurrence. | Admits a specific supplied value. | The rank is a convention, not a measurement. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.ragged-judgeability-fence` | 475<br/>*(rule 460)* | s | One genuinely-drawn-but-unobserved cell means the observation really is incomplete. | Drops the pair. | Silent continue. | **silent** |
| `mint.ragged-matrix-admission` | 464<br/>*(rule 450)* | a | Cells a Figma variant set proves it never realizes are not missing data. | Admits a pair whose holes are filled from a base observation. | A set that simply was not drawn looks the same as one that cannot be. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.saturation-caveat` | 418<br/>*(rule 405)* | a | Occurrences at or below cell count means every cell holds at most one observation, so any values would fit. | Admits the pair with an epistemic warning. | A refusal here was measured as worse than the disease. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.saturation-denominator-excludes-supplied` | 507<br/>*(rule 490)* | a | Saturation is a statement about drawn evidence, so supplied cells belong in neither denominator nor histogram. | Adjusts the caveat's numbers. | None known. | `caveats.push` |
| `mint.share-threshold` | 66<br/>*(rule 65)* | s | A literal used at three or more uniform usage sites is shared vocabulary; below three it stays a per-site leaf. | Routes into imported.shared vs a per-site path. | The only pure numeric threshold in the mint, and nothing names it or the two-site near miss. | **silent** |
| `mint.shared-name-spelling` | 246<br/>*(rule 241)* | a | A deduped literal's name is mechanical from its kind and value. | Admits a colour-family or scale name. | Two different design intents with the same value share one name. | **silent** |
| `mint.single-axis-full-coverage` | 315<br/>*(rule 306)* | s | Substituted refs expand over every declared enum value, so partial coverage would fabricate a dangling ref. | Drops an otherwise-fitting single-axis classification. | The terminal reason never says a single axis fit but coverage was partial. | **silent** |
| `mint.sparse-vacuous-fill` | 319<br/>*(rule 309)* | a | A presence-shaped channel's unobserved combinations draw nothing, so the declared vacuous value closes the dangling-ref hole. | Admits a classification full coverage would refuse. | Unlike the ragged fill, a sparse fill attaches NO caveat, so filled cells are indistinguishable from measured ones. | **silent** |
| `mint.stylename-blocks-shared-dedupe` | 681<br/>*(rule 657)* | s | A style-named leaf must not collapse into imported.shared and lose the designer's word. | Drops style-named leaves from the share threshold. | Silent. | **silent** |
| `mint.text-style-namespacing` | 108<br/>*(rule 106)* | a | A Figma text style is design-system vocabulary shared across components. | Admits a component-independent imported.text path. | The routing itself is silent; only an extensions block traces it. | **silent** |
| `mint.textstyle-identity-required-for-merge` | 655<br/>*(rule 632)* | s | Same value is not enough to merge: the text-style identity must match too. | Drops the merge and forces a suffixed sibling. | Silent. | **silent** |
| `mint.triple-root-only-full-coverage` | 544<br/>*(rule 525)* | a | Three placeholders maximum, root only, every combination observed with a single value. | Admits the three-axis classification. | An irrelevant axis can never ride along, so a near-fit falls through generically. | `reason` |
| `mint.uncorrelated-refusal` | 575<br/>*(rule 555)* | s | Values that differ across variants without correlating to any axis, pair or triple mint nothing. | Drops the whole observation; the binding stays null. | A four-axis design token has no carriage. | `reason` |
| `mint.uniform-or-nothing` | 293<br/>*(rule 286)* | a | An identical value at every occurrence is one fact and one leaf. | Admits a single leaf. | Happy path; usageSites is the only trace of how many sites agreed. | **silent** |

## Standing rules

1. **A new door needs a register entry.** Add `// @door <stage>.<name>` at the deciding rule and a row to `door-register.json`, or the gate refuses.
2. **A door may be silent, but it may not be undeclared.** `receipt: {"channel": "none"}` is an accepted, gated answer. Claiming a receipt that does not exist is not.
3. **The premise is the reviewable part.** A door with no stated premise is refused. The counter-example is where the next defect will come from.
4. **The census numbers are pinned.** A count moving in either direction is a human's decision — fewer subtractions is not automatically progress.
